extracted.intended_audience: Appeals Section staff, Review Committee members/secretaries, departmental representatives, appellants and their advisers under the Canada Pension Plan
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for initiating, preparing, conducting, and deciding appeals to Review Committees under the Canada Pension Plan, including notice content, file compilation, evidence admissibility, confidentiality, decision-making powers, and post-hearing transmissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may initiate an appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The appeal may be initiated either by the appellant himself or by the person authorized by the Minister to manage his affairs; where two parties claim benefits by virtue of contributions paid by the same contributor and the reasons are similar they may proceed by giving joint notice of appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates standing rules for who may file a notice of appeal and permits joint notices in consolidated factual circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of appeal must identify parties and key date
rubrics_metrics.description: Apart from containing a clear identification of the appellant or, if required, of the contributor by virtue of whose contributions benefits are sought, the notice of appeal must mention the date on which the appellant was notified of the decision on the first appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date mentioned is the starting point for the time limit to appeal to the Review Committee; this enables the Director General to determine timeliness and whether an extension should be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of appeal must present reasons and pertinent facts
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of appeal must present the reasons for the appeal and the facts pertinent to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement reflects the greater formality of this procedure, allows use of facts that may bring about a review, acquaints the Review Committee with the appellant's point of view, and tends to produce more complete/methodical presentations (often prepared by lawyers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice must identify appointee to act on the Review Committee
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of appeal must identify the person that has accepted the appellant's appointment to act on the Review Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practice appellants frequently neglect to include this information; omission may be raised and the appellant invited to appoint a member later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals Section must recognise an authentic notice of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: On receiving the appellant's letter, the Appeals Section first ascertains that it can be considered as amounting to a notice of appeal; for this to be the case the author must have explicitly indicated his intention to lodge an appeal and not simply expressed dissatisfaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If it qualifies, the Appeals Section acknowledges receipt by a letter advising the appellant of salient procedural points governing Committee functioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement letter must inform appellant of Committee procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Appeals Section sends a fairly lengthy acknowledgment letter advising the appellant of salient points of procedure: composition of Committee, location arrangements, opportunities to present verbally, submission of letters/affidavits/written representations, witnesses and representation, Minister's representative presence, and Committee decision possibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This letter is of considerable importance to appellants who may have little prior idea of Review Committee hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disability cases: referral to Disability Assessment Division and possible re-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: If the case involves disability the Appeals Section transmits the file to the Disability Assessment Division (DA); DA re-examines the medical file and, if data obsolescent, may require the appellant to submit to a new medical examination in accordance with section 531(2) of the CPP Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following re-examination DA determines Department's stand; if it considers appeal unjustified it drafts a memorandum summarizing medical findings with annexed copies of all medical reports used.

rubrics_metrics.name: DA memorandum and selection of Minister's representative
rubrics_metrics.description: DA prepares a memorandum over the director's signature summarizing medical findings and annexes medical reports; DA must also decide who will defend the Minister's position (often a DA physician alone or with the district office director).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The memorandum is forwarded to Appeals Section; DA may provide the Minister's representative a detailed working file (see later about copies distribution and withheld materials).

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal Services prepares the Minister's reply to the notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Appeals Section transmits the file, together with the DA memorandum, to the Legal Services of the Department, which prepares a reply to the notice of appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reply is 'prepared according to the rules of the art' and is often deliberately vague in content, not attempting to precisely justify the Minister's contestation; the Appeals Section transmits the reply over the Director General's signature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of the case file for the Committee (documents required)
rubrics_metrics.description: The file produced for the Committee (five copies) contains the documents enumerated in section 4(2) of the Rules of procedure: the application for benefits, the initial decision (accompanied by the statement of disability assessment), the appeal to the Minister under section 83, the Minister's decision on the appeal, the notice of appeal to the Review Committee and the reply to this notice of appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All participants (except the secretary) also receive copies of the CPP text (with underlining of key sections) and the Rules of procedure (with underlining of hearing procedures). The secretary receives forms, agenda and confidentiality undertakings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from the Committee's case file
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain papers likely to be found in the CPP file are excluded from the Committee's case file, such as internal memoranda, observations by members of Disability Determination Boards, correspondence concerning the application, and the medical documentation on which DA's memorandum is based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DA's medical documentation and internal observations are withheld from Committee members and the appellant; the Minister's representative alone may receive more detailed materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for file preparation (statutory vs practical)
rubrics_metrics.description: According to section 4 of the Rules of procedure all these operations must be effected within fifteen days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practice preparing the file almost inevitably takes several weeks; the 15-day statutory timeframe is difficult to adhere to except where DA already holds a recent and complete medical file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of Committee members and chairman (formation rules and timelines)
rubrics_metrics.description: The district office director appoints the Committee member for the Department and the appellant is invited to appoint his member; once both members are named the secretary calls on them to appoint a chairman within thirty days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are many indeterminate elements that may delay formation; once formed the secretary transmits the file to each member.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission of the case file to appellant and participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Officially the appellant is entitled only to receive the reply to his notice of appeal, but in practice the secretary usually transmits to the appellant, some time before the hearing, a copy of the file distributed to Committee members; the appellant thus receives the CPP text and Rules for his use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This practice helps appellants prepare though is not strictly required by the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary may meet appellant pre-hearing to explain procedure and burden of proof
rubrics_metrics.description: The secretary of the Committee, if he considers it useful, may meet the appellant before the hearing to draw aspects of procedure to his attention, remind him that the burden of proof lies on him and of his right to legal counsel or assistance at his own cost, and to reassure him about the informal atmosphere of hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secretary may also warn that Committee members are impartial and cannot testify or plead; if the appellant designated his physician/lawyer/family member as Committee member, he may be encouraged to revoke that appointment to preserve witnesses/advisors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of evidence admissible at hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of evidence admissible are oral testimony and written evidence in the form of letters, statements under oath or representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although inclusive, the Committee has not been authorized to take evidence in any form it deems suitable (unlike some administrative tribunals); the list is therefore somewhat constrained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct and structure of the hearing (model agenda and chairman duties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings generally follow the model agenda: introductory statement by the secretary, appellant's presentation and questioning by Committee and Minister's representative, Minister's presentation, concluding questions; the Committee may determine its own procedure so long as it does not interfere with the parties' right to be heard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Chairman is responsible for directing/moderating discussion and maintaining decorum while preserving the informal character of the hearing; the secretary assists with notes and procedural problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of hearings and documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The hearing is normally held in camera; the members of the Committee are obliged to preserve the confidential character of all documents and information submitted in the process; documents tabled are placed under the secretary's custody 'at all times'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the end of the hearing the three members sign an undertaking not to disclose deliberations, papers, statements or the decision except as provided by the CPP and its regulations; the purpose is to protect appellant privacy (mental health/private life information).

rubrics_metrics.name: Role and limitations of the Minister's representative regarding DA materials
rubrics_metrics.description: The Minister's representative tables the summary of the medical documentation prepared for him by DA with the Committee and offers remarks on it; no copy of this document is given to the appellant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Minister's representative thus has access to materials (and may receive multiple copies) that are not provided to the Committee members or appellant, creating an asymmetry in information disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of new evidence introduced by appellant
rubrics_metrics.description: The appellant is always free to avail himself of any new facts in his favour; if such facts are presented, the Minister's representative will usually declare they were not known to the Minister at the time the decision was rendered and avoid speculating on their effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New facts may be taken into account by the Committee; Minister's representative typically limits response to non-speculation about impact on the original decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of PAB caselaw and precedential awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Hardly any mention is made in Committee hearings of PAB caselaw even when obviously applicable to the case; Committees are often ill-equipped to interpret and apply PAB jurisprudence and sometimes deliberately disregard it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAB has repeatedly reminded Review Committees of their obligation to abide by its decisions; lack of publicity of PAB jurisprudence and Minister's reluctance to present it are contributing factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of the Review Committee's decision-making authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The Review Committee has full authority to review the Minister's decision: it can vary it or vacate it, take any action (particularly regarding payment of benefits) that the Minister might have taken under section 83, determine any question of law or fact raised, and take into account new facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In cases concerning section 63, if the Committee vacates the Minister's decision as to the existence of conditions precedent to discretionary power, it must send the case back to the Minister so he may exercise the discretion anew in light of the Committee's conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content of Committee decisions; obligation to give reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: The Committee generally formulates its decision on a special form provided for that purpose; the form gives no indication as to how it is to be filled out and Committees usually give decisions in a few lines with little coherent and balanced analysis despite being obliged to provide justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although reasons are often sparse, the PAB has held that failure to give reasons does not invalidate the decision; on appeal the PAB may substitute its own decision or affirm the Committee's while assigning reasons it deems justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Majority rule and recording of dissent
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act implicitly recognizes any one member's right to withhold assent, but the decision of the majority is considered the decision of the Committee; the decision report form must be signed by all members so a dissenting judgment must be recorded within the majority decision, if at all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dissent is not infrequent and often motivates appellants to appeal to the PAB; the practical recording of dissent may be minimal or omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission of decision, notification periods, and appeal rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The Committee's decision is transmitted in writing to the appellant, the Director General, and the Registrar of the PAB. The appellant is notified of the outcome within 48 hours and receives a form letter advising of the right to appeal to the PAB (must lodge appeal within 90 days; period may be extended on request by the PAB) and indicating Registrar address; a copy of the Rules of procedure of the PAB is enclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If decision is favorable to the appellant the form letter notifies that the Minister has the right to appeal to the PAB on the same conditions; the Director General and Minister's representative also receive copies and documents produced in evidence by the appellant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-hearing documentation and forwarding to Appeals Section and PAB Registrar
rubrics_metrics.description: The secretary forwards to the Appeals Section a complete file together with a report summarizing appellant's allegations, arguments, representative and witnesses; within 48 hours the secretary also transmits a complete file by registered mail to the Registrar of the PAB (appeal files provided to members, originals of all documents tabled, original decision, signed undertakings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The purpose is to afford the PAB Chairman an opportunity to peruse the file before deciding whether to grant leave to appeal; the Appeals Section uses the secretary's file and report (and Minister's representative recommendation) to decide whether Director General should appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: No obligation to prepare transcript or minutes of proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Despite distribution of records relating to the hearing, none of the recipients is given a transcript or minutes of proceedings; neither the regulations nor custom oblige the secretary to prepare any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notes the secretary takes serve only to assist the Committee in its deliberations and are not formal minutes available to parties or the PAB.
